s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial pain with cranial nerve involvement and skull base abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
Enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus with bone thickening and sclerosis
Soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall of the sphenoid sinus
Intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
key_facts: 83-year-old man presented with 6 months of progressive right mandibular pain
Pain radiates to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
Requires oxycodone, paracetamol, and ketorolac for relief
Empirical course of prednisone provided no benefit
Contrast-enhanced maxillofacial CT showed enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus
Bone thickening and sclerosis of the sphenoid walls, pterygoid process, and orbital apex
Focal interruption of the foramen rotundum and lateral recess wall
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI demonstrated soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall
Intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
T2-weighted images showed a markedly hypointense signal in the lateral recess
Endoscopic evaluation revealed purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess
Histopathology was negative for hyphae and neoplastic cells
Cultures grew no bacteria or fungi

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus pyocele
shortlist.why_kept: Purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess and pyocele found during endoscopic surgery

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Enlargement of the right sphenoid sinus and obstruction of the sphenoid ostium

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent inflammation of the sphenoid sinus despite negative cultures and histopathology

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Cranial nerve involvement and skull base abnormalities

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive facial pain and skull base abnormalities with soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purulent discharge in the sphenoethmoidal recess, along with imaging findings of a pyocele obstructing the sphenoid ostium and soft tissue protruding through a breach in the lateral recess wall, supports the diagnosis of a sphenoid sinus pyocele.

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus carcinoma
rejected.why: Histopathology was negative for neoplastic cells

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process rather than a syndrome characterized by painful ophthalmoplegia

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus mucocele
rejected.why: The presence of purulent discharge and the patient's symptoms suggest an infectious process, which is more consistent with a pyocele than a mucocele
